name: sol_integrations_chainlink_ccip_2
description: Missing destination chain allowlist check before Chainlink CCIP ccipSend call
question: The source file in `source` defines a sender contract that calls the CCIP router's `ccipSend` (or an internal wrapper around it) using a caller- or user-supplied `destinationChainSelector` without first validating that value against an allowlist or mapping of explicitly supported/approved destination chain selectors, allowing messages and tokens to be sent to unintended, unsupported, or malicious destination chains; this does not apply if the destination chain selector is hardcoded to a fixed constant or is checked against an allowlist/mapping before the call.
criteria: A function accepts a `destinationChainSelector` parameter and passes it directly into `ccipSend` without checking it against any allowlist or supported-chains mapping
The contract sends CCIP messages using a chain selector read from external input or storage that can be set arbitrarily, with no validation of the value before building or sending the message

A wrapper function around `router.ccipSend` forwards the destination chain selector argument straight to the router call without any conditional check like `if(!allowlistedChains[destinationChainSelector]) revert`
